argument: Within hierarchical cross-attention between a vision encoder and an LLM, restricting cross-attention to L_s selected vision encoder layers is associated with computational complexity of the cross-attention operation under reduced to O(L_l L_s d^2 + L_l N_t d^2) when L_s << N_v.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
claim: In hierarchical cross-attention between a vision encoder and an LLM, restricting cross-attention to L_s selected vision encoder layers, with L_s much smaller than the total number of vision encoder layers N_v, yields computational complexity O(L_l L_s d^2 + L_l N_t d^2), where L_l is the number of LLM layers, N_t is the number of visual tokens, and d is the hidden dimension.
conditions: L_l is the number of LLM layers
N_t is the number of visual tokens
falsifier: The complexity expression can be verified by deriving the matrix multiplications in the hierarchical cross-attention operation with L_s selected vision encoder layers.
interpretation: The evidence supports a formal proposition concerning hierarchical cross-attention between a vision encoder and an LLM.
